comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Now the card that matters rather than a hypothetical: two regions side by side are reachable as of 386c9e0, so a laptop and a devenv genuinely split the window evenly with no way to change it. Everything the card asked for still stands - a ratio per boundary, a divider that drags, the value written into composition - and the panes inside each region already have all three, so this is the same treatment one level out.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Landed, with one correction to the card. It says the value goes 'into composition, where it is already durable' - composition is NOT persisted. There is no serde on it, no writer, and no format chosen; that is still a_27QcqNxRB in backlog-hi. So a dragged boundary survives every republish and does not survive quitting the app.

Left that way rather than pulled forward, because persisting composition is a design question of its own and this is now the best argument for answering it: equal widths are a default nobody minds losing, and a width somebody chose is not.

What landed otherwise is what the card asked for. A weight per region rather than a ratio per boundary, so the arrangement stays a list - a tree over regions is the multiplexer this project is not. A boundary is named by the region on its left rather than by an index, unlike a pane divider, because a region has an id that outlives a drag and an index does not: a drag is a stream of requests and a region can close underneath one.

One thing the card did not anticipate: this is the only share Muster clamps. A pane's ratio goes to the daemon untouched because the daemon sizes its own rectangles and refuses what it cannot do. Nothing sits behind a region boundary, and a region dragged to zero leaves no divider to grab and no way back - so neither side goes below a tenth of the pair.

RegionStrip also has tests for the first time.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Two regions side by side - a laptop and a devenv - split the window evenly and there is no way to change that. Equal shares are a defensible floor, and the arrangement over regions is the one part of the layout Muster owns rather than mirrors, so nothing upstream will ever answer it.

Wants the same treatment panes got: a ratio per boundary, a divider that drags, and the value written into composition, where it is already durable. Note that this is Muster's own split tree over regions in everything but name, and the non-goal says Muster is not a multiplexer - so keep it a list with weights rather than letting it become a tree.
title: 🪟 Regions get equal widths, and nothing can resize them
